Good afternoon Senator Tipping, Chair Roeder and the other distinguished members of the Joint Standing Committee on Labor. I am Bill Brown, Director of Actuarial and Legislative Affairs for the Maine Public Employees Retirement System (MainePERS).

MainePERS is testifying against LD 1670, An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employee Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund, because it would direct MainePERS to reallocate trust funds from specific investments to a loan program in
violation of the Maine Constitution. We also are concerned that the bill as drafted conflicts with
federal plan qualification requirements and would impose unfunded liabilities on the plan, again
in violation of the Maine Constitution. As always, we offer any assistance the committee may
request surrounding this bill.
Article IX, Section 18, of the Maine Constitution states that ...all " contributions and payments
made to the (Maine Public Employees Retirement) system to provide for retirement and related
benefits shall be held, invested or disbursed as in trust for the exclusive purpose of providing for such benefits and shall not be encumbered for, or diverted to, other purposes." Referred to as
the "exclusive benefit" rule, this passage binds the MainePERS Board of Trustees to manage these funds in order to provide the benefits earned by and promised to members.

As drafted LD 1670 directs MainePERS to divert certain trust fund investments to provide low interest loans to members for home repairs, energy upgrades, the purchase of an electric vehicle and other similar purposes through a newly created Maine Public Employees Retirement
System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Fund. Specifically the bill requires MainePERS
to divest $250 million of fossil fuel investments to fund the loan program. Because LD 1670 directs MainePERS to divest from specific investments, rather than make these decisions on the
basis of sound investment criteria and fiduciary duties, it would violate Article IX, Section 18 of the Maine Constitution.

Constitutional concerns aside, certain provisions of LD 1670 are inconsistent with federal law governing what are commonly referred to as pension loans. The IRS requires that pension loans, together with any other plan loans the member might have, not exceed the greater of $10,000 or 50% of the present value of the member's accrued benefit (capped at $50,000) and that loans be repaid in full within 5 years. LD 1670 envisions loans of up to 100% of member's
cumulative retirement system contributions, capped at $25,000, with a repayment term of 10 years. Failure by a pension plan to comply with these lRS provisions endangers the qualified
plan status of the plan and the federal tax deferral of member contributions that comes with it.

To: Committee on Labor and Housing Re: Testimony in Support of LD 1670 - An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund
Hearing Date: April 22, 2025 at 1:00 PM
Dear Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder, and Members of the Committee,
My name is Daniel Oppenheim, PhD, MD, and I submit this testimony on behalf of the Alliance of Maine Health Professionals for Climate Action, a coalition of medical and public health professionals advocating for policies that protect the health of Maine people in the face of our changing climate.
We write today in strong support of LD 1670 because of its clear and direct benefits to health, equity, and climate resilience.
Home energy upgrades are a public health intervention. This legislation makes it financially possible for public employees and retirees--nearly 150,000 Mainers--to improve the comfort, safety, and efficiency of their homes. Upgrades like heat pumps, insulation, weatherization, and electrical repairs reduce exposure to indoor air pollutants from oil and gas heating systems. These pollutants--including nitrogen dioxide, carbon monoxide, and fine particulate matter--are known to worsen asthma, cardiovascular disease, and other serious health conditions, especially among children, older adults, and people with preexisting conditions.
By shifting investments out of the fossil fuel industry and into clean energy upgrades in homes across the state, this bill will reduce both household energy burdens and emissions that harm our air quality and climate. It will also reduce out-of-pocket energy expenses for retirees on fixed incomes, offering long-term financial and health security.
As health professionals, we are also excited about the ripple effects of this bill: - It will reduce reliance on dirty fuels that worsen respiratory health. - It will reduce the risk of cold-related illness in under-heated homes. - It will support hundreds of jobs in sectors that improve public health through healthier housing.
The MainePERS loan program envisioned by LD 1670 is a win for public health, a win for retirees, and a win for the climate. We respectfully urge the Committee to vote Ought to Pass on this innovative and health-forward legislation.
Sincerely, Daniel Oppenheim, PhD, MD On behalf of the Alliance of Maine Health Professionals for Climate Action Daniel.Oppenheim@mainehealth.org

To:  Committee on Labor From: David Gibson, Sierra Club Maine Chapter Volunteer Date: April 20, 2025 Re:  Testimony in Support of LD 1670, An Act to Establish the Maine Public
Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder, and members of the Committee on Labor,
I am testifying on behalf of Sierra Club Maine, representing over 22,000 supporters and members statewide. Founded in 1892, Sierra Club is one of our nation's oldest and largest environmental organizations. We work diligently to amplify the power of our 3.8 million members and supporters nation-wide. We urge you to support L.D. 1670, An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund.
I worked with Representative Kessler to draft this legislation. This is modeled after a successful program that I helped to implement a decade ago while I worked as the Energy Efficiency Specialist at the Nevada Governor's Office of Energy (NGOE). At the NGOE, we created the Direct Energy Assistance Loan (DEAL) program, which allowed state employees to borrow up to $6,000 for home efficiency improvements with 0% interest rate.1 The loans were repaid through a monthly payroll deduction. This meant that participants couldn't default on the loan without leaving state employment. The DEAL program was a huge success. Our office had to offer limited application periods because we were so flooded with applicants each time we made the program available. In its first year, it funded 119 projects, utilizing the entire $600,000 annual budget.2
In my role, I developed the list of improvements that were eligible for funding, and provided quality control inspections for a percentage of participants. When I visited homes to verify the work that was completed, people told me they could feel the difference in comfort in their homes, and were appreciative of the upfront assistance to make the improvements possible. In the first few years of the program, there were only a handful of participants who had left state employment. The program manager told me
1 Fact sheet on the Direct Energy Assistance Loan Program: https://energy.nv.gov/uploadedFiles/energynvgov/content/Programs/DEAL%20Fact%20Sheet(4).pdf 2 State of Nevada Status of Energy Report 2016: https://energy.nv.gov/uploadedFiles/energynvgov/content/About/2016_StateOfNevada_StatusOfEnergyR eport.pdf

that all of them paid off the loan in full and expressed their gratitude for being able to participate.
L.D. 1670 creates a program in Maine that expands upon the success of Nevada's DEAL program in several ways.
 This program will offer loans to all public employees and retirees in the MainePERS system, including teachers, police, firefighters, and workers at the city, county and state levels.
 This program will allow participants to borrow up to $25,000.  This program will allow funding for a variety of improvements, including energy
efficiency, solar, home repairs, or purchase of an electric vehicle.
For more than 15 years, I have led efficiency and clean energy programs, with focus on K-12 education and workforce development. These programs have reached thousands of people across multiple states. Home energy improvements offer a multitude of benefits, including improved comfort, health and safety, reduced energy costs, increased home value, and reduced risk of mortgage default. Importantly, this will reduce retirement expenses for beneficiaries, by permanently reducing their home energy expenses. Universally, the biggest barrier to achieving these benefits is the upfront cost of the improvements. This program aims to help all 150,000 MainePERS participants across the state to achieve these benefits for their homes.
While the focus is on improving the homes of PERS participants, this program offers a variety of other benefits to the state. Investing $25 million/year in home improvements will create or retain 400-500 jobs, leading to increased state tax revenue and lasting economic development. In addition, as loans are repaid, the fund will be continually replenished, enabling it to continue indefinitely with on-going multiplier effects. Offering this new benefit to public employees will increase employee satisfaction and will likely reduce employee turnover. These energy improvements will reduce carbon emissions across the state and increase resilience to storms, heat waves and cold snaps. With Federal grants being retracted and National Green Bank funding halted, this program will help Maine to achieve our climate goals set by the Governor and Legislature - while offering an example for other states to follow!
Please vote Ought to Pass on L.D. 1670.
Respectfully submitted on behalf of Sierra Club Maine,  David Gibson

Laubenstein, III President, Maine Association of Retirees SUBJECT: LD 1670, An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder, and members of the Committee on Labor. My name is William H. Laubenstein, III. I am President of the Maine Association of Retirees (MAR) whose membership includes retired State employees, retired teachers and other public service retirees.
MAR is opposed to LD 1670 which would create a home repair and energy upgrade loan program and fund. Persons eligible to obtain the low interest loans offered by LD 1670 include active and retired members of the Maine Public Employees Retirement System (MainePERS). The loan program is to be funded from allocation of retirement system portfolio funds. In addition, LD 1670 directs MainePERS to allocate annually for 10 years $25 million from portfolio funds currently invested in fossil fuel holdings.
As clearly set forth in the testimony of MainePERS at the public hearing on April 22, LD 1670 violates the Maine Constitution, Art. IX, Sec. 18, which mandates that all funds in the MainePERS portfolio be held, invested or disbursed as in trust for the exclusive purpose of providing for retirement and related benefits. In addition, directing the MainePERS to allocate funds currently invested in fossil fuel holdings impinges on the statutory authority, and fiduciary responsibility, of the Board of Trustees to administer all matters related to the operation of MainePERS, including making decisions on "...all matters pertaining to administration, actuarial assumptions, actuarial recommendations and the reserves and the investments of the retirement system and direct cash receipts as it considers appropriate..." 5 MRS, sec. 17103 (7).
MAR respectfully requests the Committee vote ought not to pass.

To: Labor Committee From: Linda Woods (Waterville) Re: Testimony in Support of LD1670: An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund Date: April 22, 2025
As a retired teacher and environmental activist, I view Earth Day as an ideal time to be writing testimony in support of a bill that would provide financial assistance for public employees and retirees statewide to reduce their carbon footprint.
LD 1670 would create a low-interest loan fund to finance the upfront cost of up to $25,000 for efficiency, clean energy, electric vehicles, or repairs to our homes. Many of us MePERS recipients are living primarily on our pension funds. While our pension checks are (most likely) adequate for our day-to-day expenses, they do not allow for any home upgrades to improve efficiency or comfort. That means many of us are spending a large portion of our monthly checks to heat our older houses. We are also unlikely to have air conditioning which is becoming a necessity based on the humidity we have been experiencing in recent summers. Having the opportunity to apply for a low-interest loan would a huge benefit to provide the upgrades people need for comfort. Yet, the cost of adding efficiency upgrades is more than we pensioners can afford. Lowering our home energy costs would lower our energy bills and reduce our overall retirement expenses. As many of us age out of our homes and look to downsize, our inefficient homes do not have the resale value of a more efficient dwelling.
LD 1670 is a low-risk investment as it calls for MainePERS to re-allocate $25 million a year for 10 years from their current fossil fuel investments. For several years I have been calling on the MainePERS Board to divest from fossil fuels. Since the Board has continued these investments, this would be a way to continue their current investment strategy while reducing the overall carbon emissions. It would also improve financial returns compared to current investments in fossil fuel industry. A 2% loan interest rate is better than the 0.43% annual fossil fuel returns over the last decade.
I urge you to vote in support of LD 1670 primarily because it would be advantageous to MainePERS beneficiaries like me and approximately 150,000 city, county, and state employees and retirees. Since Maine is trying to attract younger people to move to our state, having 400-500 jobs in the energy efficiency and home improvement sector could be an incentive to relocate to a state that is a national leader in home energy investments.

I'm writing to express my support for LD1670: An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund. I write both in my capacity as ED of passivhausMAINE and as a Mainer whose family pays into the PERS system, as my husband is a first grade teacher in Falmouth.
I appreciate the added benefit of a low interest loan for 150,000 employees who pay into the Maine PERS system, and I appreciate the focus on home improvement and decarbonisation for healthy, resilient buildings and cost savings. I especially appreciate the redirecting of invested funds away from fossil fuels and towards these benefits. LD1670 supports Maine families and households both those who are able to borrow the low interest funds and those whose businesses are enhanced by completing the work.
Injecting up to $25M/year in Maine's retrofit economy represents potentially 1000 families investing in efficiency. passivhausMAINE has a training series to train builders to complete retrofits. From grade school visits, to pre-apprenticeships to multi-day workshops, we encourage entering the trades and improving the existing building stock (450,000 units needing attention), as a comprehensive goal.
passivhausMAINE's retrofit initiative, retrofitMAINE, focuses on scaling low-income retrofits and we are always looking for sources of funding to support this work. At a time when federal funds are uncertain, investing in Mainers and keeping our dollars working in-State has my full support.
I urge the committee to vote Ought to Pass.
Respectfully submitted,,
-Naomi

Testimony of Rene Augustus La Casse in Support of LD 1670: An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home
Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund
Senator Tipping, Representative Roeder, and honorable members of the Labor Committee, I am Rene Augustus La Casse, Manager of Municipal Strategy and Policy Analyst at A Climate to Thrive. A Climate to Thrive is a community-driven non-profit that is working on a clean energy transition that prioritizes community benefits across Maine, with a particular focus on energy equity. Thank you for providing me with this opportunity to support LD 1670: An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund.
This bill seeks to create a loan program that will provide low-interest loans for home repairs and residential energy efficiency improvements that will serve current and retired employees who are a part of the MainePERS system.
The impacts of this bill will be significant, with nearly 150,000 MainePERS participants who could benefit from this program. The loans available in this program can be used for home repairs or the adoption of energy efficient technologies like heat pumps or solar panels, while also providing Mainers with opportunities to purchase an electric vehicle. Critical to the merits of this bill is that it understands the role that initial costs play in the adoption of new technologies, and in home repairs. The maximum loan is $25,000, which will help Maine homeowners adopt these new technologies and prepare their homes for cold and wet conditions.
Nevada's Direct Energy Assistance Loan (DEAL) demonstrates that this type of program can be effective, and that interest exists among public employees for this type of initiative. The program being considered in this legislation is flexible to the needs of MainePERS beneficiaries, and goes beyond the frameworks set by DEAL to ensure that beneficiaries will be able to create changes that result in a broad reduction of home energy expenses for retirees, something that will save them money for over decades.
Finally, as an organization, ACTT maintains close relationships with our municipalities, and understands the critical role that their public service plays in our ability to make positive change in our community. This bill will help public servants in our community make essential changes to their homes, ensure that public servants across our state can adopt new energyefficient technologies, and make investments and repairs that will save them money for decades. For these reasons, ACTT urges this committee to support the passage of LD 1670: An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund.

10045101:
Richard Thomas Waterville LD 1670
Greetings, Honorable Representatives, My name is Richard Thomas, and I live in Waterville, Maine. I am a retired
psychologist, and I am married to a Maine PERS member (retired teacher, Margrit Thomas). I strongly support this bill.
For the past 3 years, I have tried without success, as a member of Divest Maine, to encourage MainePERS to divest from fossil fuels, in accordance with the law passed in 2021 by this legislature (LD 99, 2021). LD 1670 would go a long way to make up for their failure to obey this Maine State law.
LD 1670 would allow Maine PERS beneficiaries to make energy conversions that would both reduce greenhouse gas emissions and save them money in the long run. Because this involves contributing to a loan fund, this money would replenish itself, rather than draining Maine PERS funds.
I support our local teachers and public employees, and want them to have this new benefit. Please vote Ought to Pass on LD 1670!
10045192:
Ruth Poland Bar Harbor LD 1670
RE: Testimony in support of L.D. 1670 "An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund" My name is Ruth Poland, and I am a teacher at the Mount Desert Island High School in Bar Harbor, where I also live with my family. I am testifying in support of L.D. 1670 "An Act to Establish the Maine Public Employees Retirement System Home Repair and Energy Upgrade Loan Program and Fund". I am a beneficiary of MEPERS and a home-owner in Bar Harbor where home prices have skyrocketed in the past five years. Since I purchased my home nine years ago, I have had to make numerous upgrades in order to maintain the integrity of the home, its insulation and air-sealing and its heating and cooling systems. I know myself and many other teachers who would greatly benefit from funding to aid in such projects. Maine has the oldest housing stock in the union, resulting in homes with high energy costs and associated emissions. These utility costs exacerbate the cost of living for middle-income families such as those who have worked for the state and public education systems. In my own school, new teachers cannot afford housing within our district and resort to purchasing run-down, far-flung homes if they can afford them at all. This bill would help make home-ownership more achievable by reducing the cost of utilities, while also shoring up the aging housing stock we currently have. In addition, this bill would help reduce carbon emissions in the state to compensate for the fact that MEPERS failed in its directive to divest from fossil fuels (LD99). For these reasons, I respectfully encourage you to support L.D. 1670. Thank you for your time and consideration of my testimony. Sincerely, Ruth Poland, Science Teacher & Sustainability Coordinator at Mount Desert Island High School
